gen-gf-corben-author: Chunky, friendly swagger with a gap-toothed grin: Corben's terminals pull back and leave a big opening, while Author sits beneath it. Corben is built to announce; Author, a text serif, is built to explain.
gen-gf-corben-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: Soft, bold and a bit show-offy, Corben has a lowercase a whose strokes vary just gently. And BhuTuka Expanded One brings curvy, unhurried letters whose joins stay as stout as the stems.
gen-gf-corben-gf-hepta-slab: Hepta Slab stretches every word out and keeps its strokes as uniform as neon tubing, with counters that breathe. Corben's gentle thick-and-thin cadence above it gives the pair its strongest quality: texture meeting a steady line.
gen-gf-corben-gf-kiwi-maru: Kiwi Maru spaces its letters generously, with terminals that stop well short of the stem and rings for o's. But Corben's quiet modulation above it never snags the eye, and that smoothness is the pair's best trait.
gen-gf-corben-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Each character in Stint Ultra Expanded seems to float off on its own, wide and pipe-cleaner thin in feel. Yet Corben is best at soft, brushlike weight shifts up top, while Stint holds its bowls at stem thickness below.
gen-gf-courier-prime-gf-cascadia-mono: Courier Prime lays down fixed-width, code-style letters with a measured beat and no calligraphic thinning anywhere in them. Cascadia Mono, a sans-serif, packs a compact skyline of curves as stout as its stems.
gen-gf-courier-prime-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One barely separates capitals from lowercase and leaves big stretches of blank space between letters. Julius Sans One drifts across a paragraph lightly, while Courier Prime's typewriter beat stays behind as a headline.
gen-gf-courier-prime-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa runs wide, with stubby ascenders and descenders next to a big x-height and curves that stay distinct. Next to Courier Prime's typewriter rhythm, it feels like a plain sans loosening a tie.
gen-gf-courier-prime-gf-lexend-giga: Courier Prime keeps a structured, fixed-width beat with no thinning in its lines, ideal for a technical headline. But Lexend Giga, a sans-serif, opens each word with generous tracking and flat, single-weight linework.
gen-gf-courier-prime-gf-lexend-mega: Courier Prime ticks along in fixed-width, code-style letters with a measured, spaced-out beat that never thins. Lexend Mega, a sans, looks drawn with one nib, with open c's and a body nearly as tall as its capitals.
